holding_summary: Grantee took title subject to lessor's covenant not to break through a party wall; equity enjoined future violations but denied a mandatory injunction to close the existing opening absent proof of substantial injury.
notes: Restrictive-covenant dispute over a party wall between department stores; no lodging/boarding content.

holding_summary: A written agreement for the owner to continue residing on her farm while the defendant worked it and shared produce did not establish an ordinary landlord-tenant relationship reserving a 'certain rent,' so the summary repossession statute did not apply.
notes: Farm-labor/support agreement between owner and worker; not a dwelling-letting or lodging arrangement.

holding_summary: Theater chairs and curtains installed by a lessee were removable trade fixtures, not part of the leasehold, and passed to the sheriff's-sale purchaser of those goods rather than to a later purchaser of the leasehold.
notes: Commercial trade-fixture priority dispute over a theater lease; no relation to residential lodging.

holding_summary: Land lying within the bed of a laid-out but unopened street remains taxable to its private owner until the city actually opens the street for public use.
notes: Municipal tax-exemption dispute over an unopened street; unrelated to lodging.

holding_summary: Statutory provisions letting a coal company condemn a neighbor's land for a private tramway and mine entries were unconstitutional, both as outside the act's title and as a taking of private property for private use beyond the police power.
notes: Coal-mining eminent-domain/police-power case; no lodging or boarding content.

holding_summary: An order refusing all liquor licenses in the county, reciting a full hearing and reasons tied to public necessity, was not shown to be an abuse of the quarter sessions' statutory discretion and was affirmed.
notes: Concerns discretion to grant/refuse liquor licenses for inns and taverns; does not address the legal character or regulation of lodging/boarding arrangements themselves.

holding_summary: An order granting a retail liquor license after hearing was affirmed where the record showed compliance with statutory procedure and nothing impeached its regularity.
notes: Companion liquor-license procedure case; not about lodging-house legal character or regulation.

holding_summary: A franchised lighting company could not cut off service to a new owner of commercial premises for a prior tenant's unpaid bill absent actual or constructive notice of a rule requiring payment of arrearages.
notes: Utility-service dispute between successive store occupants; no lodging or boarding issue.

holding_summary: A city ordinance declaring it a nuisance to keep hogs outside designated districts was a valid police-power measure, even where the plaintiff's piggery predated the surrounding residential development.
notes: Municipal nuisance regulation of hog-keeping; unrelated to lodging or letting of rooms.

holding_summary: The Fairmount Park Commission's statutory authority to appoint park guards was independent of the city's civil-service acts, so guards appointed without civil-service examination were lawfully employed.
notes: Municipal civil-service/park-governance dispute; no relation to lodging.

holding_summary: Where a grantor conveyed a lot with the right to build over an adjoining four-foot alley up to the grantor's then building line, the grantee acquired no right to build over a later extension of the alley when the grantor moved his own building forward.
notes: Deed/easement boundary dispute over a private alley; no lodging content.

holding_summary: An executor's bare power of sale did not authorize him to lease devised real estate for more than three years without the devisees' written authorization, so the leases, and their claimed ratification by acceptance of rent, were void under the Statute of Frauds.
notes: Executor's authority to lease commercial office rooms; not a residential lodging arrangement.

holding_summary: A husband's equity bill to enjoin his wife from interfering with his use of land, where she was in possession of the marital home by his original consent, was in substance an ejectment action better resolved at law, so the injunction was reversed.
notes: Marital dispute over occupancy of the family home; not a compensated letting/lodging arrangement.

holding_summary: A first-class township's commissioners lacked express or implied statutory authority to enact an ordinance forbidding the feeding of garbage to animals within the township.
notes: Township police-power/ordinance-authority case concerning animal feeding; unrelated to lodging.

holding_summary: A borough could, in good faith under its police power, refuse to let a franchised electric company plant poles on one particular street while offering a nearby alley instead, notwithstanding its ordinance's general consent to street use.
notes: Utility pole-placement/franchise dispute; no relation to lodging or boarding.

holding_summary: A judgment for a boarding house guest injured in a stairway fall was reversed for insufficient evidence, since the hallway lights had been extinguished by someone other than the landlord and the plaintiff herself testified there was no hole in the carpet that caused her fall.
notes: Negligence suit against a boarding house keeper turning entirely on evidentiary sufficiency; the opinion never addresses the legal character (lease/license/lodging) or regulation of the letting arrangement, only a passing reference to defendant's occupation as boarding house keeper.

holding_summary: Where land was conveyed bounded by a private alley that was open and in use at the time of sale, the right to use the alley passed as appurtenant to the grantee absent language excepting it from the grant.
notes: Deed-boundary/easement dispute over a private alley; no lodging content.

holding_summary: A lease clause giving the tenant 'first privilege' to rent the building for a further three-year term, inserted because the tenant was buying the outgoing tenant's business, entitled him to a three-year extension at the original rent without any change in terms.
notes: Commercial storefront lease-renewal dispute; not a residential lodging arrangement.
